title: A Summit for the Monsoon
premise: Felix Joubert has spent a decade flying medicine and gossip into a rain-soaked coastal interior, keeping her past as carefully hidden as her landing strips. When an unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave etched with maps and journals in her grandmother's handwriting, Felix learns the wilderness she thought was hers was actually inherited—and that a mining syndicate's surveyor, Idris Okonkwo, has been hunting the same cave for months. Stranded together by the monsoon, they must survive on a leaking boat, navigate the glacier route before calving season seals it, and decide whether the cave's legacy belongs to the family that hid it or the valley that kept its secrets. The story ends with Felix choosing to stay: she files the cave as a protected heritage site under the valley collective's name, burns her own escape plan, and finally lets herself be known.
about_author: Emrys Vasquez is a former floatplane mechanic who spent six years in remote coastal communities before turning to fiction. Their writing explores how landscapes hold memory longer than people do.

chapters.title: The Weight of Weather
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A routine med-flight through worsening weather establishes her competence, isolation, and the valley's dependence on her—while she deflects every personal question with practiced ease. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as self-sufficiency.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. An abnormally low tide reveals a cave mouth below her usual fuel cache; inside are waterproofed journals and hand-drawn charts in her grandmother's script. She recognizes the handwriting and panics. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past surfacing literally at her feet.

chapters.title: The Stranger on the Beach
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Introduce the surveyor whose skiff wrecked near the cave; he claims to be a botanist but his instruments say otherwise. Felix finds him half-drowned and, against instinct, hauls him aboard. Emotional beat: wary hospitality masking mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Monsoon Lockdown
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm closes every pass; the airstrip floods and Felix's plane takes debris damage. They're trapped together in her stilt cabin with the journals between them. Emotional beat: claustrophobia and forced intimacy.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Hand
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Reading the journals by lamplight, Felix learns her grandmother mapped the caves deliberately—not for treasure, but to document a network the family used to smuggle people out during an old purge. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Surveyor's Confession
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Cornered by evidence, Idris admits he works for Meridian Extraction, which wants the cave system's mineral rights—but he's begun doubting his employers after finding records of what the caves sheltered. Emotional beat: shame and the first crack of honesty.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. With the plane grounded, their only route out is her grandfather's old boat, hull soft with rot. Repairs become a negotiation of trust; Idris proves useful with his hands. Emotional beat: grudging partnership forming under shared labor.

chapters.title: Rumors Fly Faster Than Planes
chapters.summary: Village elder Marta's POV. Word reaches the settlement that strangers were seen at the cave; Meridian's advance team arrives asking questions. Marta, who owes Felix's grandmother a debt, sends a coded warning. Emotional beat: the community as silent guardian.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Meridian's team boards Felix mid-supply-run, searching her cargo and probing about 'anomalous survey data.' She lies fluently and realizes invisibility is over either way. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Chart That Lies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Felix and Idris discover the journal charts contain deliberate errors—a cipher only someone raised on her grandmother's stories could read. Idris offers his geology training to help decode it. Emotional beat: alliance cemented by shared purpose.

chapters.title: Night Run Upriver
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They slip out ahead of Meridian's second team, running the flooded river at night in the patched boat. A near-capsize forces Felix to trust Idris completely for the first time. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into trust.

chapters.title: The Valley Keeps Its Dead
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Sheltering in an abandoned homestead, Idris reads more journals and confronts what his company erased here decades ago—including a village his own grandfather helped clear. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden, not just birthright.

chapters.title: Sabotage at the Cache
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They find their supply cache burned and the boat's spare parts stolen—Meridian is closing the net. Felix's escape fantasy (flying out alone, disappearing again) dies hard. Emotional beat: rage giving way to acceptance that flight is no longer possible.

chapters.title: Marta's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta meets Felix secretly and reveals the valley collective has quietly held ancestral title claims all along; what's missing is documentation—which the journals provide. She asks Felix to stop hiding. Emotional beat: belonging offered, terrifyingly.

chapters.title: The Glacier Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The only remaining route to the registry office crosses the glacial moraine, passable only before calving season. They race a warming forecast, hauling the boat over ice. Emotional beat: hope with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A storm pins them on the ice for two days; Idris develops hypothermia and Felix keeps him alive by telling him her real history aloud—the first time she's told anyone. Emotional beat: vulnerability as survival tool.

chapters.title: Meridian Catches Up
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Meridian's team intercepts them at the moraine's edge; Idris stalls them by claiming the cave data is worthless without his decryption, buying hours. His betrayal of his employers becomes irreversible. Emotional beat: burning bridges as liberation.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. As the glacier begins to calve behind them, they make the final crossing under collapsing seracs, the boat lost to a crevasse, arriving on foot with nothing but the journals sealed in wax. Emotional beat: everything expendable except the truth.

chapters.title: The Registry Office
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the coastal town, they file the heritage claim with the collective's name on it, backed by the journals and Marta's testimony. Meridian's lawyers descend—but the claim holds long enough to freeze extraction permits. Emotional beat: quiet triumph, hard-won.

chapters.title: What Idris Chose
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Offered reinstatement and a promotion to make it all go away, Idris refuses and hands over internal Meridian documents to the collective's lawyers, ending his career. Emotional beat: redemption priced honestly.

chapters.title: A Summit for the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Back home, the valley gathers at the cave mouth for a naming ceremony; Felix speaks her grandmother's name aloud and her own history with it. The monsoon breaks like applause. Emotional beat: belonging claimed at last.

chapters.title: Flight Plans
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, epilogue. Months later, Felix flies the repaired mail run with passengers now—Marta's grandchildren, visiting researchers, Idris heading to testify. She leaves the cabin door unlocked and the cave marked on public charts. Emotional beat: visibility chosen, inheritance passed forward.
